title: Playlet choreographer: convert maintenance runbooks into idempotent admin playlets
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Build a 'playlet choreographer' service that converts existing textual maintenance runbooks into executable, idempotent admin playlets that can be scheduled, dry-run, and audited from the Console. Background: Oncall and SRE teams repeatedly run ad-hoc shelllets and scripts stored in Google Drive/Confluence; these are hard to test, not idempotent, and lack telemetry. The choreographer will: 1) parse a playlet manifest (typed inputs + preconditions), 2) provide a dry-run simulator, 3) execute with permission checks and RBAC gates, 4) emit structured telemetry and action provenance, 5) support automatic rollback hooks and canary steps. Success criteria: create a v1 manifest spec, ship a dry-run simulator in the internal sandbox, convert three high-frequency runbooks into playlets, and demonstrate reduced mean time to remediate (MTTR) in a pilot. Constraints: must work with Private deployments (playlet Exec must respect VPC policies), limited ops IAM surface, and must never run destructive steps without explicit Approval token. Integrations: Console runbook panel, Dedicated autoscaler rollback hooks, operator audit logs, and the admin-runner sidecar. Deliverables: manifest spec (Confluence), choreographer service (Go), dry-run harness (JS CLI), telemetry plumbing (instrumentation + dashboard).
